lede: A fortnight ago Robert D'Arcy was a rank, a burial and a rumour of Yorkshire, and his family was a list of names on a tree. He now has a marriage, a career in five gazetted steps, a funeral reported in seventeen newspapers — and a household. This page assembles it.
parents: First commissioned 1778 as Practitioner Engineer and Second Lieutenant, Corps of Engineers · Major 1802 · Lieutenant-Colonel 1 March 1805 · Colonel 1813 · Major-General by 1827 · died Chatham 13 May 1827, buried there with military honours on the 19th, aged 76
Baptised SOUTH LEITH, Midlothian, 19 July 1754, daughter of JOSEPH WARD and MARTHA GAIRDEN · buried Chatham 1823, aged 66

children.note: Royal Artillery from about 1795. St Domingo 1793, Sicily, Walcheren, and five years in Persia in the service of Prince Abbas Mirza. Lieutenant-Colonel, K.L.S. Died at Home Mead, Lymington, 7 February 1848, leaving his property to his wife Catherine and five children.

39th Foot. Married MISS LUDLAM OF GUERNSEY, announced September 1805 in a notice calling him “son of Lieut. Colonel D'Arcy”. Peninsular War 1808. In Ireland with the regiment 1820 and 1822. Married secondly Maria, and sailed for New South Wales on the convict ship England in April 1826. THE LINE THIS ARCHIVE DESCENDS FROM.

Married JOHN MADDOCK JONES of Pen-y-bryn, Ruabon, Major of the Royal Denbigh Militia, at Chatham in 1806, her brother JOSEPH signing as witness. She died at Le Havre in February 1843 and he at Ingouville near Havre the following month. Her death notice calls her “daughter of the late MAJOR-GENERAL D'ARCY, R.E.” — the only record anywhere that gives Robert a corps as well as a rank.

Aged 57 and living in Joseph's house at Priestlands in 1841. Of exactly the right generation, in exactly the right household — and no other record of him has been found anywhere in Hampshire. Portsea's transcript stops in 1782, so a baptism of 1784 could never have been found in it.

Son of Robert and Jane, christened in Barbados while his father served there. Gentleman Cadet to Second Lieutenant, Corps of Royal Engineers, 1 February 1804; First Lieutenant 1 March 1805, in the same Ordnance Office announcement that made his father a Lieutenant-Colonel. Buried Chatham St Mary, 9 May 1805, aged nineteen. The Kentish Gazette of 14 May calls him “the son of Col. D'Arcy, chief engineer of Chatham lines” and says he was interred with military honours — the same words used of his father twenty-two years later.

Daughter of Robt. D'Arcy and Jane, christened in the same Barbados parish two years after Constantine. She is not on the family tree and appears in no other record found so far. Robert and Jean had at least six children.

portsea: Only one of them was baptised at Portsea, and this archive spent months reading that as meaningful. It is not: FindMyPast's Hampshire collection covers Portsea St Mary continuously from 1770 to 1792 and returns Joseph and nobody else — so the others were christened wherever the Corps had posted him. A regiment moves; a parish register does not follow it. AND THIS ARCHIVE HAD ALREADY FOUND WHERE TWO OF THEM WERE, AND HAD NOT PUT IT HERE. Constantine was christened at St Michael, Barbados in 1786 and Jane in the same parish in 1788 — inside the twenty-four-year gap between Robert's first commission and his next gazetted promotion. That has been on the Hornby page since the summer while this page called Constantine unplaced.
shape: Two sons in the artillery and the infantry, a third in his father's own Corps of Engineers who died at nineteen, two daughters, and a brother in the house at the end. It is the ordinary shape of a successful service family, scattered across three continents by the postings that made it, and every part of it was invisible to this archive a fortnight ago.
open: Robert's own parentage. Seventeen newspapers announced his death and not one named a relative — though four other notices now name four of his children as his.
Whether Richard was his son, which needs a baptism from a parish this archive has not yet identified.
What became of JANE D'ARCY, christened in Barbados in 1788 and untraced after it.
When Robert went to Barbados and when he came home. The christenings of 1786 and 1788 are the only evidence he was ever there, and his career between 1778 and 1802 is otherwise blank.
And who ELIZABETH PITT was — living in Joseph's house in 1841, dying at Lymington in 1851, and sharing a surname that ran through four generations of this family.
